answers.question: Question 1: No tools were defined, so here is the smallest tool set I propose, each with what it can return. Please confirm it. (1) List orders: returns each of the signed-in customer's orders, cancelled ones included, with its refund or none; or gets no answer. (2) Cancel order (order number): answers cancelled, not cancellable with the order's status, order not found, or gets no answer; cancelling an order already cancelled answers cancelled. (3) Issue refund (order number): returns the order's one refund (pending, issued, or failed on a lasting error), creates none on a passing error, or gets no answer; repeated calls return the same refund. (4) Staff follow-up (order number, reason): creates a task for store staff and answers created, or gets no answer, and is not sent again. Its reasons are refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, and one I add: refund amount differs, for the case where the refund call returns an amount other than the one the customer said yes to.
answers.recommended: Yes: these four tools, with the reason refund amount differs added to the staff follow-up.
answers.reply:
No. The record says:
> | Order system | Lists the customer's orders, cancels an order, and issues the refund for an order. | Harbor Goods | None. |
> | Staff task queue | Takes the follow-up tasks the agent creates for store staff. | Harbor Goods | None. |
> Q3 How does the agent know the order belongs to the person asking? Recommended: the customer is already signed in, and the agent sees only that customer's orders (a precondition).
> - Refund status: pending, issued, failed.
> - Rules, not fields: full-order cancellation only (no partial); refund amount = order total paid; refund payment method = order's payment method; at most one refund per order.
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> Q2 How does the agent hand off to the manual refund process? Recommended (a): a state-changing handoff call, e.g. request_manual_refund(order_number, reason), creating a task for store staff.
> Q3 Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off. For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> - One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 2: The order system has no docs, so I compared two of its behaviours with common order systems. First: in common systems a call that gets no answer may still have done its work. If a cancel call with no answer may have cancelled the order, the agent sends it once more (safe, since cancelling a cancelled order answers cancelled) and never refunds an order whose cancellation it cannot confirm. Second: in many systems a list read right after a write may not show it yet. If the order list shows a refund as soon as the refund call made it, then after a refund call with no answer, a list that shows no refund means no refund was made, and the agent asks staff to issue it; if the list can lag, the agent cannot tell, and asks staff to check instead, so staff never issue a second refund. Does a cancel call with no answer possibly cancel the order, and does the order list show a refund as soon as it is made? Claims put to the owner: C-18, C-44.
answers.recommended: Yes to both: a cancel call with no answer may have cancelled the order, and the order list shows a refund as soon as the refund call made it.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> | Order system | Lists the customer's orders, cancels an order, and issues the refund for an order. | Harbor Goods | None. |
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> Q3 Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off. For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 3: When the cancel call gets no answer, the agent sends it once more. If that also gets no answer, the shortest path is: the customer says yes; the cancel call gets no answer; the agent sends it again; again no answer. What does the agent do then?
answers.recommended: It sends no refund call, creates a staff follow-up task with the reason cancellation unknown, and tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled, that no refund was made, and that store staff will follow up.

answers.question: Question 4: Three calls can fail where nothing in the inputs says what the agent tells the customer. (a) The order list call gets no answer before anything is proposed. (b) The cancel call answers order not found for an order the agent just read. (c) The staff follow-up call gets no answer, and it is not sent again. What does the agent do in each?
answers.recommended: (a) It says it cannot look up the orders right now and changes nothing. (b) It says the order could not be cancelled and changes nothing. (c) It tells the customer what it knows about the order and the refund, says it could not pass the case to store staff, and asks them to contact the store.
answers.reply:
